Let me analyze this OIML certificate.

Certificate details:

- Project number: 1901431

- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V. (OIML Issuing Authority NL1)
- Address: Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, the Netherlands
- Person responsible: C. Oosterman
- Person title: Head Certification Board
- Phone: +31 78 6332332

- Website: www.nmi.nl
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Applicant:
- Minebea Intec GmbH, Meiendorfer Strasse 205 A, D-22145 Hamburg, Germany

Manufacturer: same as applicant (labeled "Applicant and Manufacturer")

Certified type:
- Category: "Load cell"
- Type designations: PR 6246
- Module designation: "Analog load cell"? The cert says "A tension load cell, with strain gauges." That's an analog load cell. Hmm, but rule says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. The load cell with strain gauges is analog. But don't fabricate — the cert doesn't explicitly say "Analog load cell". I'll set it to null or maybe "Analog load cell". Actually strain gauge load cells are analog, but the certificate doesn't state that explicitly. Safer: null. Hmm, but the schema has "Analog load cell" as option. I'll use null since not explicitly stated. Actually, "with strain gauges" implies analog, but let's not fabricate. Use null.

- Description: "A tension load cell, with strain gauges."

Model family: The characteristics table has two columns:
- Emax: "100 kg up to 200 kg" and "200 kg up to and including 3000 kg"
- n: 2000 and 6000
- Y: 10000 and 20000
- Z: 2000 and 8000

So the cert covers two capacity ranges. These are ranges, not discrete models. Hmm. So how to model? The table has two columns representing two Emax ranges. This is like a config/model axis: capacity range.

Option 1: Model family with two models: "Emax=100-200kg" and "Emax=200-3000kg". The varying attributes are max capacity, n, Y, Z.

The rule 4 example with R60 shows Emax values 25,30,50,60,75,90 as discrete models. Here we have two ranges. I think modeling as model_family with 2 models is appropriate:
- model_id: "Emax=100-200kg" (label maybe "100 kg up to 200 kg")
- model_id: "Emax=200-3000kg"

model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: per model, value {min: 100, max: 200} unit kg; {min: 200, max: 3000} unit kg
- max_number_of_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 2000 vs 6000 (dimensionless)
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 10000 vs 20000
- ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: 2000 vs 8000

Type-level characteristics:
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg
- accuracy_class: C
- rated_output: 2.0 mV/V (convert comma decimal: 2,0 → 2.0)
- input_impedance: 650 Ω ± 6 Ω → how to structure? Could be value 650, unit "Ω", with a tolerance. Maybe add a characteristic input_impedance_tolerance: 6 Ω. Or value "650 ± 6" with unit "Ω". The strict structured value: value: 650, unit_symbol: "Ω" and a separate attribute input_impedance_tolerance: 6 Ω. I'll do that.
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 55}, unit "°C"
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7 (dimensionless)
- humidity_class: CH
- safe_overload: 150, unit "%" with reference Emax → safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- output_impedance: 610 Ω, output_impedance_tolerance: 0.5 Ω
- recommended_excitation: 4-24 V, AC/DC → split: recommended_excitation_voltage: {min:4, max:24}, unit "V"; excitation_type: "AC / DC"
- excitation_maximum: 28 V, AC/DC → value 28, unit "V"; note AC/DC. Maybe include excitation_maximum_type: "AC / DC". Or keep simple.
- transducer_material: Stainless steel
- atmospheric_protection: Hermetically welded

Recommendation:
- id: R60, edition: 2000, amendment: null, scheme: A? The certificate number R60/2000-NL1-17.63 — scheme A is typical for R60 certs issued under MAA. Actually OIML CS: certificates under scheme A are for measuring instruments (type evaluation), scheme B for modules. Load cell certs under R60 are Scheme A. The schema says scheme (A|B). I'll put "A". accuracy_classes: ["C"].

Test reports:
- NMi-1901431-01, dated 30 October 2017, 68 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
- NMi-1901431-02, dated 30 October 2017, 74 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
- NMi-1901431-03, dated 30 October 2017, 68 pages, role: type_evaluation_report

Revision history: none present.

Footnotes: none.

DoMC documents: R 60 DoMC-01 rev.0 and R 60 DoMC-02 rev.0 — additional national requirements from the United States. Where to record? Maybe not in schema; could add in characteristics type_level? Not a characteristic. I could omit, or add as a note. The schema doesn't have a field. I'll skip, or maybe include in certified_type description? Hmm. Rules say don't fabricate but also omit fields not present. I could add these to... there's no obvious slot. Perhaps add them in matrix_tables? No. I'll just omit or mention in description. Actually I could add to recommendation? No. Let me leave them out of structured fields but maybe include in certified_type.description? The description field is "free-text description if present" — the description present is "A tension load cell, with strain gauges." I'll keep it as that and maybe extend with the DoMC note? Better keep it faithful. I could add "notes" — but not in schema; adding extra fields is risky but usually tolerated. The instruction says produce JSON following the layered schema; extra fields might break strict validators. I'll keep to schema. Actually, I might include the DoMC info in test_reports as additional documentation? Role "documentation_file"? They're declarations, not reports. Hmm, DoMC-01 and DoMC-02 are "Declarations of Mutual Confidence" documents. Could record as test_reports with role "documentation_file"? That's a stretch. I'll omit them.

Actually, maybe better to include them somehow since they're meaningful. But schema adherence is priority. I'll omit.

Page total: 2 (page 1 of 2, page 2 of 2).

Certificate date_issued: 2017-11-03.

Now the matrix table: I should also record the characteristics table in matrix_tables? Rule 4: extract 2-D tables as matrix_tables AND populate model_family/model_level. The table here is 2-column with type-level constants (colspan) and varying rows. I can record a matrix_table capturing the two-column structure. Let me do:

matrix_tables: [
  {
    "name": "Characteristics of the load cell",
    "columns": ["maximum_capacity", "max_number_of_load_cell_intervals_nlc", "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin", "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr"],
    ... hmm the columns are actually capacity ranges.
  }
]

Actually the table columns are: characteristic | range 1 | range 2. So rows are attributes. Let me structure:

{
  "name": "Characteristics of the load cell",
  "columns": ["attribute", "Emax 100 kg up to 200 kg", "Emax 200 kg up to and including 3000 kg"],
  "rows": [
    {"attribute": "maximum_capacity", "range1": "100 kg up to 200 kg", "range2": "200 kg up to and including 3000 kg"},
    ...
  ]
}

Hmm, that's awkward. Maybe better:

columns: ["maximum_capacity_kg", "n", "y", "z"] with rows being the two ranges:

rows: [
  {"maximum_capacity_kg": {min:100,max:200}, "n": 2000, "y": 10000, "z": 2000},
  {"maximum_capacity_kg": {min:200,max:3000}, "n": 6000, "y": 20000, "z": 8000}
]

That's cleaner. Name: "Characteristics of the load cell by capacity range". Include description noting remaining attributes are common across ranges.

Model IDs: "Emax 100–200 kg" — avoid unicode issues? JSON handles unicode fine. I'll use "Emax=100-200kg" and "Emax=200-3000kg" following the example style "Emax=25t".

For maximum_capacity model_level values: value as {min, max} object. That's allowed per rule 2 ("Ranges ... become {min, max}").

Footnote markers: none.

"The characteristics for n_max, Y and Z can be reduced separately." — This is a note. Could be a footnote? It's not a footnote with marker. Could include as a characteristic note or in matrix description. I'll put in matrix_tables description or omit. Maybe add to certificate-level? I'll include in matrix table description.

Accuracy class: C (single class).

Scheme: "A".

Edition: 2000. Amendment: null → omit (rule 8: omit if not present). Actually amendment field could be omitted.

certificate.oiml_issuer_id: "NL1".

Let me also include "module_designation": null — the load cell with strain gauges... R60 certs often state "analog load cell" but here not explicitly. I'll set null.
